title: Transwell migration assay to interrogate human CAR-T cell chemotaxis
author: Oner, Kobold
materials: x: Number of cells in experimental wells
y: Number of cells in baseline wells

steps.title: Calculate blood volume
steps.instruction: Determine the volume of whole blood to process by calculating the number of T cells needed for transduction on day 2, add one extra for a non‑transduced control, and multiply the total by 1.8.

steps.title: Dilute whole blood
steps.instruction: Add one part phosphate‑buffered saline (PBS) to the whole blood (1:1 dilution) and mix gently with a serological pipette.

steps.title: Dispense density gradient medium
steps.instruction: Pipette 15 mL of Histopaque‑1077 (or equivalent density‑gradient medium) into each sterile 50 mL conical tube (each tube can accommodate up to 35 mL of diluted blood).

steps.title: Layer diluted blood onto gradient
steps.instruction: Carefully layer the diluted blood onto the Histopaque‑1077 by holding the tube at a 45° angle, leaning against the side, and slowly releasing the blood so that the interface between the two layers is not disturbed.

steps.title: Centrifuge gradient
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes at 1,000 × g for 20 min at 20 °C in a swinging‑bucket rotor with the brake set to 0.

steps.title: Collect and wash PBMCs
steps.instruction: Using a serological pipette, transfer the PBMC layer into new 50 mL conical tubes, fill each tube with PBS and centrifuge at 520 × g for 15 min at 20 °C (default brake). Aspirate the supernatant, discard, and resuspend each pellet in 5 mL PBS. Pool all donor PBMCs into a single 50 mL tube, bring to volume with PBS, and count cells with a hemocytometer or automated counter.

steps.title: Initial centrifugation for enrichment
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the pooled PBMCs at 520 × g for 10 min at 20 °C.

steps.title: Resuspend in MACS buffer
steps.instruction: Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cell pellet in 80 µL cold MACS buffer per 10⁷ cells.

steps.title: Add CD3 Microbeads
steps.instruction: Vortex the CD3 Microbeads for 15 s, add 20 µL of beads per 10⁷ cells, mix by pipetting up and down, and incubate 15 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Wash labeled cells
steps.instruction: Add 2 mL cold MACS buffer per 10⁷ cells, then centrifuge at 300 × g for 10 min at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare LS column
steps.instruction: Attach an LS Column to a compatible MACS separator, place a 50 mL conical tube beneath to collect flow‑through, and apply 3 mL cold MACS buffer onto the column.

steps.title: Resuspend cells for loading
steps.instruction: After the wash centrifuge, discard supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 500 µL cold MACS buffer; add an additional 50 µL buffer for every 10⁷ cells exceeding the first 10⁸ cells.

steps.title: Load and wash column
steps.instruction: Load the cell suspension onto the LS column and allow it to flow through completely. Wash the column with 3 mL cold MACS buffer, repeat the wash two more times (total three washes).

steps.title: Elute pan T cells
steps.instruction: Discard the flow‑through, place a new 50 mL conical tube under the column, apply 5 mL cold MACS buffer, immediately insert the plunger and push moderately to recover the labeled pan T cells.

steps.title: Final buffer addition and count
steps.instruction: Add 25 mL cold MACS buffer to the eluted cells and perform a final cell count.

steps.title: Calculate Chemotactic Index
steps.instruction: Compute the Chemotactic Index (ChI) by dividing the number of cells in the lower chamber of each experimental condition (x) by the average number of cells in the lower chambers of the baseline (control) conditions (ȳ): ChI = x / (1/n ∑ᵢ yᵢ).

steps.title: Calculate Normalized Cell Index
steps.instruction: For each well w at time t, calculate Normalized Cell Index (NCI) as NCI_w(t) = CI_w(t) / CI_w(t_norm), where CI_w(t) is the cell index at time t and CI_w(t_norm) is the cell index at the last time point before cytotoxic treatment.

description: The protocol below describes the strategy we implemented to increase T cell trafficking into solid tumors. Specifically, we made use of the C-X-C motif chemokine receptor 6, (CXCR6), expressed alongside a chimeric antigen receptor targeting mesothelin, a cell surface glycoprotein, which, among others, has been found to be highly expressed in pancreatic tumors. The assessment tools detailed here, although described in this specific context, can be adapted to determine the migratory potential of otherwise modified T cells (i.e., another chemokine receptor, such as CCR8) or T cells in general (Cadilha et al., 2021). Along the same lines, the chemoattractant detailed here, CXCL16, the exclusive ligand of CXCR6, can be replaced with another chemoattractant of choice.
